title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the dossier concerns an abstract formalism of correspondences and 'Poincaré–Hodge algebras', i.e. graded commutative algebras with Poincaré duality, a Lefschetz-type class and positivity, as a testing ground for the standard conjectures. The neighbouring pages are an unrelated typescript (Shatz-style cohomology of group schemes) misfiled in the dossier, so this page has to be read on its own. The model algebra here is the exterior algebra ΛV of an even-dimensional vector space, as for the cohomology of an abelian variety (H* = ΛH¹).

First attempt (crossed out). Take a non-degenerate φ ∈ Λ²V̌, i.e. a symplectic form, and its square χ = φ² ∈ Λ⁴V̌, viewed as χ: Λ⁴V → k. He apparently wanted to regard χ as a quadratic form on Λ²V, then abandoned this.

Second example. Take a non-degenerate χ' ∈ Λ⁴V̌. 'Non-degenerate' should mean that Q = Q_{χ'}, Q(a,b) = χ'(a∧b), is a non-degenerate symmetric bilinear form on Λ²V. Take α = id, so the auxiliary space W̃ equals Λ²V. Within the formalism, elements ξ ∈ W̃ = Λ²V produce any desired φ up to scalar, hence any non-degenerate φ̌ ∈ Λ²V up to scalar; φ̌ is the dual/inverse bivector.

Now form φ̌² in two ways:
- in the algebra ΛV ⊗ ΛV, using Λ²V ⊂ V⊗V, landing in Λ²V ⊗ Λ²V;
- in ΛV itself, as the image under the product Λ²V ⊗ Λ²V → Λ⁴V, giving φ̌^(2) ∈ Λ⁴V.

Pull φ̌^(2) back to Λ²V ⊗ Λ²V by the coproduct component Λ⁴ → Λ²⊗Λ². Then use Q to identify Λ²V with its dual. The result is an endomorphism u of Λ²V. This is a composite construction ξ ↦ φ ↦ φ̌ ↦ φ̌^(2) ↦ u, of Hodge-star/Lefschetz type.

Claim (asserted, not proved). The orbits of ξ and of φ̌ under u can be infinite once dim V ≥ 4 (or 6?), V of even dimension. The marginal adds that both orbits are infinite and, apparently, of unbounded dimension.

Purpose: a counterexample showing that a natural iterative operation in the abstract formalism does not have finite or periodic behaviour. Presumably this tests whether some finiteness or algebraicity expected for operators built from the Lefschetz and duality data can follow from the axioms alone.
errors: The hesitation '≥ 4 (ou 6?)' is justified. For dim V = 4, Λ⁴V is a line and the Λ²⊗Λ² component of the coproduct of a volume element is (up to scalar) the canonical tensor of the wedge pairing on Λ²V (Klein quadric). After identification by Q (also the wedge pairing up to scalar), u is a scalar. Orbits are then trivial up to scalars, so the claim can only hold for dim V ≥ 6.
Infiniteness of the orbits is asserted without proof. It is plausible for generic data in dim ≥ 6, but not verified on the page.
Several words are illegible (e.g. 'deux conventions'), so the exact meaning of ξ, W̃ and α depends on preceding pages not supplied.

ideas.what: Square of a symplectic form φ² ∈ Λ⁴V̌ and of its inverse bivector, used to build quadratic forms on Λ²V (Klein-quadric-type pairing)
ideas.modern_name: Pfaffian / wedge-pairing on Λ²V; Hodge-star–type operators

ideas.what: Exterior algebra ΛV as a model Poincaré–Hodge algebra (cohomology of an abelian variety) for testing the abstract formalism of the standard conjectures
ideas.modern_name: abstract Lefschetz/Poincaré-duality algebras; Lefschetz standard conjecture for abelian varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck 1969 (Standard conjectures), Kleiman 1968; Lieberman 1968 for abelian varieties
ideas.where_published: Standard conjectures are in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968/1969); the Poincaré–Hodge algebra formalism itself is not published as such

ideas.what: Endomorphism u of Λ²V built from φ̌^(2) ∈ Λ⁴V via coproduct and the form Q_{χ'}, with a claim that orbits of ξ, φ̌ under u can be infinite for dim V ≥ 6
ideas.modern_name: counterexample to finiteness of an iterated duality/Lefschetz-type operator

missed.claim: An explicit check that, in an abstract Poincaré–Hodge exterior-algebra model, a natural operator built from Lefschetz/duality data has infinite orbits. This would show that the relevant finiteness cannot follow from the axioms alone. The dimension threshold (4 vs 6) and the proof are left open.
missed.quote: Je dis que l'orbite sous u des éléments ξ et φ̌ de Λ²V peuvent être infinis, si dim V ≥ 4 (ou 6?)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It illustrates the limits of purely axiomatic (Poincaré/Lefschetz algebra) approaches to the standard conjectures, a theme of current work on Lefschetz algebras and abstract Hodge structures. It is a small unproved remark, not a result.

deep.surprise_reason: A small exploratory linear-algebra example with an unproved claim about infinite orbits in an exterior-algebra model. It is interesting only as a glimpse of how Grothendieck tested the abstract Poincaré–Hodge formalism; it contains no substantial new result.
transcription_corrections: 'φ̌^(2) par Λ²V⊗Λ²V → Λ⁴V' more likely reads 'φ̌^(2) image par Λ²V⊗Λ²V → Λ⁴V' (the product map).
The marginal '(qui est ∈ Λ⁴V)' qualifies φ̌² regarded via the product; the line 'Λ̇V est l'image de ⊂ Λ̇V⊗Λ̇V' is garbled; the sense is 'à l'image de … ⊂ Λ̇V⊗Λ̇V ; le carré de φ̌ dans Λ̇V'.
'Utilisant la forme Q = Q_{χ'} définie par χ'' — 'Utilisant la' at the line end precedes 'forme'; fine.
The final marginal lines are uncertain; they seem to read 'les deux orbites infinies, et plus encore … de dim non bornée (quand dim V croît …)'.
